paper_title: Pi in the Sky: Neutron Stars with Exceptionally Light QCD Axions
coupling_convention: f_a in GeV (converted by me from the paper's epsilon = (m_a/m_a^QCD)^2 constraint using m_a^QCD * f_a = 5.7e6 eV*GeV, i.e. m_a^QCD = 5.7 ueV * (1e12 GeV / f_a))
notes: Paper constrains exceptionally light QCD axions (axion-gluon coupling) in the epsilon-m_a plane, presented in the f_a-m_a plane in Sec. VI. The combined exclusion (abstract; Tables IV, V, VII) is 5e-7 <~ epsilon <~ 0.2 for m_a >~ 2e-9 eV (conservative Scenario A: cooling excludes epsilon > 5.2e-7, glitches/thermal relaxation up to ~0.17-0.2). Since the exclusion is a BAND in epsilon at fixed m_a, the emitted points trace both band boundaries: the first 5 points are the lower f_a boundary (epsilon = 5e-7) and the last 5 the upper f_a boundary (epsilon = 0.2), forming a closed excluded band between them. Upper mass extent set by SN cooling bound (m_a below tens of meV); I truncated at 1e-2 eV. This is an astrophysical (neutron star structure/cooling/glitch) bound, not a DM haloscope, so no local DM density assumption. No statistical CL stated; 0.95 is nominal.
